title: 六州歌头·东风着意
title_en: Liu Zhou Ge Tou: The East Wind Takes Care
author: 韩元吉

form.zh: 词（六州歌头，双调一百四十三字）
form.en: ci lyric to the tune Liu Zhou Ge Tou, two stanzas, 143 characters

text_note.zh: 资料库本子的断句是“隐映新妆，面临水岸”和“草软莎平跋马，垂杨渡、玉勒争嘶”，这里按通行的断句改为“隐映新妆面，临水岸”和“草软莎平，跋马垂杨渡，玉勒争嘶”。第一句的“着”，资料库作“著”，是同一个字的旧写法。“燕支”也有本子写作“燕脂”，都是胭脂的意思。
text_note.en: The database text breaks two passages differently. Here they follow the usual reading: the 'new made-up face' line ends with miàn (face), and 'grass soft' ends before bá mǎ (turning the horse). The first line's zhuó is written with an older form of the same character in the database. Yān zhī (rouge) also appears in some editions with a different second character; both mean rouge.

readings.zh: 着意：读 zhuó yì，用心、特意。不读 zháo 或 zhe。
readings.en: Read zhuó yì: to take care, to do on purpose. Not zháo or zhe.

readings.zh: 莎：读 suō，莎草，一种长在水边、地上的草。不读 shā。
readings.en: Read suō here: sedge, a grass. Not shā.

readings.zh: 燕支：读 yān zhī，就是胭脂。燕不读 yàn。
readings.en: Read yān zhī: rouge. Here the first character is yān, not yàn (swallow).

readings.zh: 薄：单用时口语读 báo；也有人按书面语读 bó。
readings.en: báo in everyday speech; some read it bó as in written words.

glosses.zh: 着意：用心，特意。
glosses.en: zhuó yì: with care, on purpose.

glosses.zh: 小桃：一种早开的桃花。
glosses.en: xiǎo táo: an early-blooming peach.

glosses.zh: 红粉腻：粉红的花瓣细腻柔润，像女子脸上的胭脂粉。
glosses.en: hóng fěn nì: pink petals, smooth and soft, like rouge on a girl's face.

glosses.zh: 娇如醉：娇艳得像喝醉了酒一样泛红。
glosses.en: jiāo rú zuì: lovely and flushed, as if tipsy.

glosses.zh: 倚朱扉：靠着红色的门。扉，门。
glosses.en: yǐ zhū fēi: leaning against a red door. Fēi means door.

glosses.zh: 年时：当年，那时候。
glosses.en: nián shí: in that year, back then.

glosses.zh: 隐映新妆面：桃花和她刚化好妆的脸互相映照，若隐若现。这里化用了唐代崔护“人面桃花相映红”的诗意。
glosses.en: yǐn yìng xīn zhuāng miàn: the peach blossoms and her freshly made-up face shine on each other. It echoes Cui Hu's Tang line about a face and peach blossoms glowing red together.

glosses.zh: 春将半：春天快过一半了。
glosses.en: chūn jiāng bàn: spring was nearly half gone.

glosses.zh: 夹城：城外另筑的城墙，两边有墙，中间是路。
glosses.en: jiā chéng: a walled road built alongside the city wall.

glosses.zh: 莎：莎草，一种草。
glosses.en: suō: sedge, a kind of grass.

glosses.zh: 跋马：勒住马，让马掉头。
glosses.en: bá mǎ: to rein in the horse and turn it.

glosses.zh: 垂杨渡：长着垂柳的渡口。
glosses.en: chuí yáng dù: a ferry landing with weeping willows.

glosses.zh: 玉勒：用玉装饰的马笼头，代指马。
glosses.en: yù lè: a jade-decorated bridle, standing for the horse.

glosses.zh: 争嘶：一匹匹马争着嘶叫。
glosses.en: zhēng sī: horses neighing one after another.

glosses.zh: 蛾眉：像蚕蛾触须一样细长弯弯的眉毛，代指美丽的女子。
glosses.en: é méi: long curved eyebrows like a moth's feelers, standing for a beautiful woman.

glosses.zh: 凝笑：含着笑，笑意停在脸上。
glosses.en: níng xiào: a smile that stays on her face.

glosses.zh: 脸薄：脸皮薄，容易害羞。
glosses.en: liǎn báo: thin-skinned, shy.

glosses.zh: 拂燕支：脸上像抹了一层胭脂，指害羞脸红。燕支，胭脂。
glosses.en: fú yān zhī: as if brushed with rouge, meaning she blushes. Yān zhī means rouge.

glosses.zh: 绣户：装饰华丽的门窗，指女子的住处。
glosses.en: xiù hù: a beautifully decorated door, meaning a lady's room.

glosses.zh: 曾窥：曾经偷偷看过。
glosses.en: céng kuī: once peeked at.

glosses.zh: 依依：舍不得分开的样子。
glosses.en: yī yī: reluctant to part.

glosses.zh: 共携手处：从前一起手拉手走过的地方。
glosses.en: gòng xié shǒu chù: the places where we once walked hand in hand.

glosses.zh: 香如雾：花香像雾一样弥漫。
glosses.en: xiāng rú wù: the scent of flowers spreads like mist.

glosses.zh: 红随步：落下的红色花瓣跟着脚步。
glosses.en: hóng suí bù: red petals follow our footsteps.

glosses.zh: 怨春迟：埋怨春天来得太慢。
glosses.en: yuàn chūn chí: complaining that spring comes too slowly.

glosses.zh: 消瘦损：人消瘦了很多。
glosses.en: xiāo shòu sǔn: grown very thin.

glosses.zh: 凭谁问：有谁来问一问呢？
glosses.en: píng shuí wèn: who will ask about it?

glosses.zh: 泪空垂：白白地流泪。
glosses.en: lèi kōng chuí: tears fall for nothing.

glosses.zh: 堂前燕：住在屋前的燕子。
glosses.en: táng qián yàn: the swallows nesting in front of the hall.

glosses.zh: 烟雨：像烟雾一样的细雨。
glosses.en: yān yǔ: misty rain.

glosses.zh: 佳期：美好的约会，相聚的日子。
glosses.en: jiā qī: a happy meeting, a lovers' date.

glosses.zh: 前度刘郎：上次来过的刘郎。唐代刘禹锡被贬多年回到京城，写诗说“前度刘郎今又来”，看桃花。传说东汉刘晨进天台山采药，遇到仙女，回家后再也找不到。这里诗人用来说自己旧地重游。
glosses.en: qián dù liú láng: Master Liu who came here before. The Tang poet Liu Yuxi came back to the capital after years away and wrote about returning to see the peach blossoms. A legend also tells of Liu Chen, who met fairy maidens in the mountains and could never find them again. The poet means himself, returning to an old place.

glosses.zh: 几许：多少。
glosses.en: jǐ xǔ: how many.

glosses.zh: 风流地：留下美好往事的地方。
glosses.en: fēng liú dì: places of happy, romantic memories.

glosses.zh: 应悲：应该也会伤心。
glosses.en: yīng bēi: must also feel sad.

glosses.zh: 暮霭：傍晚的云雾。
glosses.en: mù ǎi: evening mist.

glosses.zh: 目断：望到看不见为止。
glosses.en: mù duàn: gazing until nothing more can be seen.

glosses.zh: 武陵溪：陶渊明《桃花源记》里武陵渔人顺着溪水找到桃花源，后来再也找不到。这里指和心爱的人相会的地方。
glosses.en: wǔ líng xī: Wuling Stream. In Tao Yuanming's Peach Blossom Spring, a fisherman of Wuling followed a stream to a hidden land and could never find it again. Here it means the place where the lovers met.

glosses.zh: 难追：追不回来。
glosses.en: nán zhuī: cannot be brought back.

translation.en: The east wind seems to take special care,

translation.zh: 先吹到了小桃树的枝头。
translation.en: and reaches the little peach tree first.
The pink petals are smooth and soft,
lovely and flushed as if tipsy,
leaning by a red door.
I remember that year:

translation.zh: 桃花映着她刚化好妆的脸，
translation.en: peach blossoms glowed with her freshly made-up face,
there on the river bank.
Spring was nearly half gone,
and the sun through the clouds was warm.
I turned past the slanting bridge
to the west of the walled road.
The grass was soft and the sedge was smooth.

translation.zh: 我在垂柳边的渡口勒马回头，
translation.en: At the willow ferry I reined in my horse,
and the horses neighed one after another.

translation.zh: 我认出了那位含笑的美丽女子，
translation.en: I knew that beautiful girl with her quiet smile.

translation.zh: 她害羞得脸上泛起红晕。
translation.en: She was shy, and her cheeks blushed as if with rouge.

translation.zh: 我曾经在她华美的门窗前偷偷看过她，
translation.en: I had once peeked at her by her fine door,

translation.zh: 分别时依依不舍，满心遗憾。
translation.en: and parting left a lingering ache.

translation.zh: 我们一起手拉手走过的地方，
translation.en: In the places where we walked hand in hand,
the scent of flowers spread like mist,

translation.zh: 红色的花瓣跟着脚步飘落，
translation.en: and red petals followed our steps.

translation.zh: 那时还埋怨春天来得太慢。
translation.en: Back then we complained that spring came too slowly.
Now I have grown thin,
and who will ask why?
Only the peach blossoms know,
and my tears fall for nothing.
The swallows that nested by the hall long ago
fly through the misty rain
in pairs once more.
People grow old,
but spring stays lovely forever,

translation.zh: 我只能在梦里和她相会。
translation.en: and I can meet her only in dreams.

translation.zh: 我像那旧地重游的刘郎，
translation.en: Like Master Liu, I come back to an old place.

translation.zh: 那么多留下美好往事的地方，
translation.en: So many places of happy memories,

translation.zh: 连桃花也应该为我伤心吧。
translation.en: even the peach blossoms must grieve for me.

translation.zh: 只见傍晚的云雾茫茫一片，
translation.en: I see only the endless evening mist,

translation.zh: 我望断了那条通往桃花源的武陵溪，
translation.en: and I gaze until I can no longer see the Wuling Stream,
for the past can never be brought back.

background.zh: 这首词通篇写桃花：东风里的小桃、映着人脸的桃花、刘郎看过的桃花、武陵溪边的桃花源。诗人借桃花，写自己对多年前一位女子的思念。上半首回忆当年春天在桃花边和她相遇，下半首写如今旧地重游，人已不见。词里的女子是谁、写于哪一年，都不清楚。
background.en: This lyric is about peach blossoms from start to end: the early peach in the east wind, peach blossoms glowing with a girl's face, the peach blossoms Master Liu saw, and the Peach Blossom Spring by Wuling Stream. Through them, the poet writes of a woman he loved years ago. The first half remembers meeting her among the blossoms one spring. The second half tells of coming back to the same place, where she is gone. We do not know who she was or when the lyric was written.

author_note.zh: 韩元吉（1118—1187），字无咎，号南涧，南宋词人，做过吏部尚书这样的大官。他和陆游、辛弃疾都是好朋友，常常写诗词互相赠答。他的词多数写得雄健，关心国家，但这首写爱情的词却非常细腻柔美。
author_note.en: Han Yuanji (1118–1187), also called Nanjian, was a Southern Song lyric poet. He rose to high office, becoming Minister of Personnel. He was a good friend of Lu You and Xin Qiji, and they often sent poems to each other. Most of his lyrics are strong and full of care for the country, but this love lyric is very soft and delicate.

appreciation.zh: “六州歌头”这个词牌句子短、节奏急，一般用来写慷慨悲壮的事，韩元吉却用它写柔情，这就很特别。短短的三字句一句接一句，像一个人急急地翻着回忆：桃花、红门、水边、斜桥、垂柳、嘶叫的马，还有那个含笑脸红的姑娘。到了下半首，节奏还是那么急，心情却变了：花香还在，燕子又双双飞来，春天年年都好，只有人老了，爱人不见了。最后诗人站在傍晚的雾里，望着找不回的“武陵溪”。桃花一直开着，往事却追不回来，美景越美，心里越空。
appreciation.en: The tune Liu Zhou Ge Tou has short lines and a fast beat. It was usually used for bold, tragic themes. Han Yuanji uses it for tender love, and that makes it special. The short three-character lines come one after another, like someone quickly turning through memories: peach blossoms, a red door, the riverside, a slanting bridge, willows, neighing horses, and a girl smiling and blushing. In the second half the beat is just as fast, but the mood changes. The flower scent is still there, the swallows fly back in pairs, and spring is lovely every year. Only the man has grown old, and his love is gone. At the end he stands in the evening mist, gazing at a Wuling Stream he can never find again. The peach blossoms keep blooming, but the past cannot be caught. The lovelier the view, the emptier his heart.
